I moved the attack to retaining an elastic reference state while covalent bonds rearrange inside the load-bearing units. This supplied an actual chemical mechanism and a discriminating result: a closed bullvalene reaction network can repeatedly redistribute its internal states without changing which external handles remain connected, but compliant polymer attachments largely screen that motion from the material.

The strongest completed result is therefore a physically constrained design principle, with a molecular calculation behind it. It does not justify a new bullvalene hydrogel proposal or further tuning of isolated reaction rates. The guide results, constitutive discriminator and failed thioester construction remain intact.

Bullvalene’s Hardy–Cope rearrangements change internal carbon connectivity while retaining the covalent attachments to its substituents. This chemistry and its incorporation into polymers are established prior art. The recent fluorinated-bullvalene study supplies a particularly useful starting point: an explicit isomer network, calculated structures and transition states, and experimental evidence that mechanical loading changes isomer populations.

Two qualifications are essential:

Bounded internal rearrangements do not automatically guarantee a useful modulus. Chemical equilibration can strongly soften a network, and a connected network can have floppy modes. The equilibrium modulus must still be positive.
This derivation has fixed coarse connectivity. External partner exchange changes the network compatibility problem. It needs an actual mechanism that transports or restores the relevant reference information; the equation does not supply one.

For the cage construction, the external handles physically retain coarse connectivity, and the internal span inventory is bounded. The calculated equilibrium shear modulus remains positive. That is a concrete instance of repeated internal bond rearrangement with a retained elastic reference, under the stated assumptions.

This classification is a useful extension of the earlier constitutive discriminator: it identifies both which reaction cycles can erase organisation and which allowed reactions actually participate in carrying load.

The conventional alternative is already strong

Protein unfolding and refolding provides an independently demonstrated way to retain a covalent backbone while repeatedly changing internal structure. It also supplies a much larger recoverable length change.

The ferredoxin-like protein hydrogels are particularly informative. They exhibited substantial recoverable hysteresis, with roughly 60% returning within two seconds and the remainder recovering more slowly. Their transient quasi-plastic deformation shows why retention of the backbone does not guarantee rapid restoration of mechanical function. Aggregation of unfolded domains also participates in the material response. 
PMC

A different protein–polymer construction localises domain unfolding near highly stressed crack regions while leaving most of the material’s protein inventory folded. That is a strong alternative for repeated loading: it preserves much of the available reserve by avoiding unnecessary activation. It should not be interpreted as proof that every activated domain resets immediately. 
nature.com

Bullvalene itself also has substantial materials prior. Moreover, a paper published on 23 October reports that low bullvalene incorporation changes crystallite organisation in conjugated polymers and, after crosslinking, improves crack-onset strain while retaining comparable electronic mobility. Consequently, a generic claim that fluxional units improve packing or stretchability is already occupied. 
onlinelibrary.wiley.com

Scientific decision

I am retaining closed intramolecular exchange as an acquired chemical route, but rejecting dilute bullvalene hinges in a compliant network as the main material proposal. That decision follows from the coupled mechanical calculation and strong existing alternatives, not merely from the size of one numerical improvement.

The enabling principle worth carrying forward is:

Preserve the mechanically relevant reference information through complete reaction cycles, and calculate how strongly those cycles participate in the load-bearing degrees of freedom.

This permits original bond identities to disappear where they are unnecessary. It also prevents two false positives: a rapidly exchanging material whose useful reference geometry drifts, and a perfectly retained molecular inventory whose rearrangements scarcely affect the material.

For a stronger architecture, the required operation is now specific: repeated restoration of load-bearing organisation through changes in collective contacts, while retaining the necessary reference geometry. An isolated cage’s reaction graph does not acquire those collective contacts. A static improvement in initial morphology does not establish their restoration after repeated deformation.

The completed molecular model, population-independent coupling bound, finite-extensibility test and reference-cycle criterion give a concrete basis for that next construction. Further isolated rate tuning has no scientific justification until the surrounding contacts supply appreciable, recoverable mechanical participation.

I moved the attack to retaining an elastic reference state while covalent bonds rearrange inside the load-bearing units. This supplied an actual chemical mechanism and a discriminating result: a closed bullvalene reaction network can repeatedly redistribute its internal states without changing which external handles remain connected, but compliant polymer attachments largely screen that motion from the material.

The strongest completed result is therefore a physically constrained design principle, with a molecular calculation behind it. It does not justify a new bullvalene hydrogel proposal or further tuning of isolated reaction rates. The guide results, constitutive discriminator and failed thioester construction remain intact.

A chemical mechanism that retains something useful

The collective function I selected is recoverable stress redistribution with a retained elastic reference, rather than preservation of every original bond.

A preliminary graph construction exposed another obstruction. The move

AB+BC⟶AC+BCAB+BC\longrightarrow AC+BCAB+BC⟶AC+BC

preserves connectivity when performed atomically. But two overlapping transactions can each rely on the bond the other removes: both original edges of A−B−CA-B-CA−B−C can become A−CA-CA−C connections, isolating BBB. The supporting connection needs physical protection during the transaction. Ordinary associative chemistry does not automatically provide that protection.

I therefore examined intramolecular rearrangement within an intact molecular cage. Bullvalene’s Hardy–Cope rearrangements change internal carbon connectivity while retaining the covalent attachments to its substituents. This chemistry and its incorporation into polymers are established prior art. The recent fluorinated-bullvalene study supplies a particularly useful starting point: an explicit isomer network, calculated structures and transition states, and experimental evidence that mechanical loading changes isomer populations. ACS Publications+1

Here the retained organisation has a physical location:

  • The polymer handles and their coarse network connections retain the elastic framework.
  • Internal cage rearrangements provide a bounded set of alternative geometries.
  • Thermal equilibration restores the internal population after unloading.
  • Individual carbon–carbon bond identities need not survive.

This acquires internal reconfiguration. Severed-handle repair remains outside the construction.

One model for chemistry, conformation and transmitted force

I reconstructed the published network of 120 isomers and 180 transition-state labels, including its parallel reaction pathways. I used the deposited coordinates to obtain the separation of the two core-attached methylene carbons, rather than assigning an independent mechanical stroke to each reaction. The available ground-state structures span approximately 0.284–0.611 nm at those attachment points. figshare.com

For the first controlled material model, a cage sits between flexible polymer handles. Let:

Preparation and reset were included

For the bulk calculation, I used an affine network whose strand vectors are quenched from the equilibrium cage-plus-handle ensemble:

This removes a freely chosen initial stretch distribution. It is an explicit idealised preparation rule, not a simulation of the gelation chemistry.

Direct propagation through repeated extension–hold–release–hold cycles reached a repeatable periodic state without manually restoring the isomer populations. In one specified calculation—L=9.8 nm2L=9.8\,\mathrm{nm^2}L=9.8nm2, a 0.30.30.3-nm extension step and 20-second holds—the cycle dissipated approximately 4.8×10−6kBT4.8\times10^{-6}k_BT4.8×10−6kB​T per cage after settling. The population difference between successive cycles fell below 2×10−92\times10^{-9}2×10−9 in total variation by cycle ten.

That establishes a complete repeatable cycle within this model. Its very small mechanical output is consequential.

The timing is less secure than the equilibrium conclusion. The deposited conformer coordinates are not individually matched to the selected minimum energies; I used symmetry-consistent representative spans and checked their variation. I also corrected the supporting script’s approximate Hartree conversion consistently across the relative energies. Those corrections barely change the mechanical amplitude but appreciably change calculated times. The seconds above are model times, not measured polymer relaxation times.

The result keeps the possible exception visible. A sufficiently stiff surrounding structure can make the cage matter. But the tested route obtains that coupling by approaching full handle extension. It does not combine strong participation with a large remaining flexible reserve.

These calculations retain rigid isomer geometries and omit matrix packing. They cannot establish loaded kinetics in a polymer glass. What must be retained through exchange

The more general result is that chemical turnover, connectivity retention and elastic-memory retention require different state descriptions.

Suppose a reaction e:i→je:i\to je:i→j changes a mechanical reference coordinate by ded_ede​. For a complete reaction cycle CCC, define

DC=∑e∈Cde.D_C=\sum_{e\in C}d_e.DC​=e∈C∑​de​.

If every cycle has DC=0D_C=0DC​=0, there is a state function aia_iai​ such that

dij=aj−ai.d_{ij}=a_j-a_i.dij​=aj​−ai​.

Repeated chemical cycling then cannot accumulate reference displacement.

If some cycle has DC≠0D_C\ne0DC​=0, the same coarse chemical label can recur after the reference geometry has shifted. In a model with accessible, translation-repeating pathways, that permits accumulated slip. A bond-count or chemical-occupancy model can miss it entirely.

The relevant coordinate need not contain every microscopic detail. For a harmonic network,

U(x,s;γ)=κ2∥Bx+γb−a(s)∥2+G(s),U(x,s;\gamma) = \frac{\kappa}{2} \|Bx+\gamma b-a(s)\|^2+G(s),U(x,s;γ)=2κ​∥Bx+γb−a(s)∥2+G(s),

where xxx describes internal node displacements and γ\gammaγ is imposed strain, eliminating xxx gives

Ueff(s;γ)=κ2∥P[γb−a(s)]∥2+G(s).U_{\mathrm{eff}}(s;\gamma) = \frac{\kappa}{2} \|P[\gamma b-a(s)]\|^2+G(s).Ueff​(s;γ)=2κ​∥P[γb−a(s)]∥2+G(s).

Here PPP projects onto deformations that cannot be removed by internal node motion.

The mechanically relevant retained quantity is therefore PaPaPa, rather than every component of aaa, still less every original bond identity. Changes that are mechanically compatible can be extensive without erasing the chosen elastic information.

Two qualifications are essential:

  1. Bounded internal rearrangements do not automatically guarantee a useful modulus. Chemical equilibration can strongly soften a network, and a connected network can have floppy modes. The equilibrium modulus must still be positive.
  2. This derivation has fixed coarse connectivity. External partner exchange changes the network compatibility problem. It needs an actual mechanism that transports or restores the relevant reference information; the equation does not supply one.

For the cage construction, the external handles physically retain coarse connectivity, and the internal span inventory is bounded. The calculated equilibrium shear modulus remains positive. That is a concrete instance of repeated internal bond rearrangement with a retained elastic reference, under the stated assumptions.

This classification is a useful extension of the earlier constitutive discriminator: it identifies both which reaction cycles can erase organisation and which allowed reactions actually participate in carrying load.

The conventional alternative is already strong

Protein unfolding and refolding provides an independently demonstrated way to retain a covalent backbone while repeatedly changing internal structure. It also supplies a much larger recoverable length change.

The ferredoxin-like protein hydrogels are particularly informative. They exhibited substantial recoverable hysteresis, with roughly 60% returning within two seconds and the remainder recovering more slowly. Their transient quasi-plastic deformation shows why retention of the backbone does not guarantee rapid restoration of mechanical function. Aggregation of unfolded domains also participates in the material response. PMC

A different protein–polymer construction localises domain unfolding near highly stressed crack regions while leaving most of the material’s protein inventory folded. That is a strong alternative for repeated loading: it preserves much of the available reserve by avoiding unnecessary activation. It should not be interpreted as proof that every activated domain resets immediately. nature.com

Bullvalene itself also has substantial materials prior. Moreover, a paper published on 23 October reports that low bullvalene incorporation changes crystallite organisation in conjugated polymers and, after crosslinking, improves crack-onset strain while retaining comparable electronic mobility. Consequently, a generic claim that fluxional units improve packing or stretchability is already occupied. onlinelibrary.wiley.com

Scientific decision

I am retaining closed intramolecular exchange as an acquired chemical route, but rejecting dilute bullvalene hinges in a compliant network as the main material proposal. That decision follows from the coupled mechanical calculation and strong existing alternatives, not merely from the size of one numerical improvement.

The enabling principle worth carrying forward is:

Preserve the mechanically relevant reference information through complete reaction cycles, and calculate how strongly those cycles participate in the load-bearing degrees of freedom.

This permits original bond identities to disappear where they are unnecessary. It also prevents two false positives: a rapidly exchanging material whose useful reference geometry drifts, and a perfectly retained molecular inventory whose rearrangements scarcely affect the material.

For a stronger architecture, the required operation is now specific: repeated restoration of load-bearing organisation through changes in collective contacts, while retaining the necessary reference geometry. An isolated cage’s reaction graph does not acquire those collective contacts. A static improvement in initial morphology does not establish their restoration after repeated deformation.

The completed molecular model, population-independent coupling bound, finite-extensibility test and reference-cycle criterion give a concrete basis for that next construction. Further isolated rate tuning has no scientific justification until the surrounding contacts supply appreciable, recoverable mechanical participation.
